name: GE HealthCare Technologies Inc.

profile.description: GE HealthCare Technologies, spun off from General Electric in January 2023 and headquartered in Chicago, makes medical imaging systems (CT, MR, molecular imaging, X-ray), ultrasound, patient care solutions (monitoring, anesthesia, diagnostic cardiology) and pharmaceutical diagnostics (contrast media and radiopharmaceuticals) [5]. Q3 2026 revenue rose 7.2% (6.2% organic) to $5.5B, adjusted EPS rose to $1.34 from $1.07, and management raised FY2026 guidance to ~4% organic growth and $4.95-5.05 adjusted EPS [1]. The stock trades at $76.57 (52-week range $58.75-$89.77) for a ~$34.6B market cap and pays a token $0.145/yr dividend (~0.2% yield) [5].

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Since the 2023 spin-off GEHC has refreshed its imaging lines and built out Pharmaceutical Diagnostics, which grew 13% to $846M in Q3 2026; CEO Peter Arduini has centred the growth strategy on AI and precision care [1][2]. This is a significant repositioning but not a business-model transformation. AI Deployment (2/2): GEHC ships AI-enabled imaging products (deep-learning reconstruction, automated workflow) and reports the industry's largest portfolio of FDA-authorized AI-enabled devices, and Arduini is pitching a cloud-first AI orchestration platform for imaging enterprises [3][2]. Market Share (2/2): GEHC is a top-three global player in CT, MR, ultrasound and patient monitoring, and every segment grew in Q3 2026 with Advanced Imaging Solutions up 6.1% to $3.9B [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): A $23.7B backlog gives revenue visibility, but specific next-generation launches with dates and revenue targets were not disclosed [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): TTM R&D is 6.5% of revenue ($1.26B in FY2025), at or below medtech peers [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): The purpose 'Creating a world where healthcare has no limits' ties the business to patient access and outcomes and is referenced in strategy, but it is only three-plus years into independent existence and not yet validated by long consistency [4]. Community Impact (1/2): GEHC runs a published ESG program with climate goals and healthcare-access initiatives and is a UN Global Compact signatory, but no distinctive dollar-quantified charitable program was found [4][6]. Employee Retention (0/2): No tenure or voluntary turnover data was found; review-site culture ratings are excluded under the rubric [2]. Insider Buying (1/2): FMP insider statistics record 8 open-market purchases and no sales in Q2 2026, but no purchases in Q3 2026 and no dollar amounts that would show meaningful CEO-level conviction [5].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (dividend yield ~0.2% is below the 2% Dividend threshold), 10 weight units. D/E of 89.6% scores 0.91, and TTM ROE of 16.1% scores 1.0 at 2x weight [5]. Q3 2026 revenue growth of 7.2% scores 0.91, but the 2020-2025 revenue CAGR of only 3.7% ($17.16B to $20.63B) scores 0.58 at 2x weight [5]. Forward P/E of 13.9 (price $76.57 / FY2027 consensus EPS $5.50) scores 1.0, while TTM net margin of 8.5% scores 0.43 [5]. FMP's forward PEG of 1.97 scores 0.52 at 2x weight [5]. Weighted 7.44/10 rounds to 7. Liquidity is very high at ~3.4M shares/day (~$263M daily).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): IMMUNE. GEHC's revenue comes from FDA-regulated physical scanners, monitors and injectable contrast/radiopharmaceutical agents that software cannot substitute; AI instead improves image quality and scan throughput, raising the value of the installed base [3][1]. The main AI-related risk is competitive (Siemens Healthineers, Philips and software-only imaging AI vendors competing for the orchestration layer Arduini is targeting), not substitution [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI features are bundled into device pricing and GEHC does not disclose quantified AI revenue, so the tiebreaker is withheld [1].

infinite_game.summary: GEHC has a genuine patient-centred purpose and a CEO who has invested in AI and pharmaceutical diagnostics while deleveraging a spin-off balance sheet [1][2]. Through Sinek's lens it is still proving itself: the cause has only three years of independent history, the spin was a corporate-finance event rather than a cause-driven reinvention, and there is little evidence of exceptional trust or an explicit learn-from-rivals posture.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Healthcare has no limits' is service-oriented, idealistic and resilient beyond any single modality, and leadership ties AI and precision-care investment to it [4][2]. It has not yet been tested through decades or a major crisis as an independent company.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Arduini has kept R&D at ~$1.2-1.3B a year through the spin and debt paydown (interest expense fell from $542M in 2023 to $450M in 2025) while expanding AI and pharmaceutical diagnostics, and he has held a disciplined tuck-in M&A stance rather than buying growth [5][2]. These are sound long-term choices but not yet a pattern of costly sacrifices.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): The 54,000-person organization has been stable since the spin under a CEO who returned from a decade leading Integra LifeSciences, and Arduini speaks of deliberately shaping culture [2][5]. No tenure or turnover data was found to evidence an exceptional Circle of Safety.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Becoming an independent company in 2023 and pivoting toward AI-enabled, cloud-delivered imaging and radiopharmaceuticals shows adaptation [2][1]. The core business of designing and servicing imaging hardware is unchanged, so the shift is evolutionary.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): GEHC competes in a three-way imaging oligopoly with Siemens Healthineers and Philips, but no management commentary was found crediting rivals' strengths as a driver of self-improvement; messaging centres on GEHC's own platform leadership [2].

investment_thesis: GEHC delivered a clean Q3 2026: revenue up 7.2% (6.2% organic) to $5.5B with every segment growing, adjusted EBIT margin up 180bps to 16.6%, adjusted EPS of $1.34 versus $1.07, and FY2026 guidance raised to ~4% organic growth and $4.95-5.05 adjusted EPS [1]. A $23.7B backlog (~4.3 quarters of revenue) and 1.03x book-to-bill support near-term visibility, and at ~13.9x FY2027 consensus EPS of $5.50 the valuation is undemanding for a business whose physical, FDA-regulated products are structurally protected from AI substitution [1][5]. ROE of 16.1% and FMP forward PEG of 1.97 round out a solid financial profile [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is slow structural growth and leverage. Revenue compounded only 3.7% a year from 2020 to 2025, TTM net margin is 8.5%, and D/E of ~90% with negative tangible book value reflects spin-off debt and goodwill [5]. Organic orders grew just 4.0% in Q3 and backlog slipped from $23.9B to $23.7B, signalling that the strong Q2 order intake has normalized [1]. China procurement and tariff exposure remain swing factors for imaging, and the Inspire Impact Score of -73 (MISALIGNED: embryonic stem cells, IVF) is a meaningful concern for faith-based investors even though it carries no weight in the score.
key_catalysts: Raised FY2026 outlook: organic revenue growth ~4% (from 3-4%), adjusted EPS $4.95-5.05 (from $4.80-5.00) and adjusted EBIT margin of 15.5-15.7% after Q3's 16.6% margin [1]
Pharmaceutical Diagnostics momentum, with Q3 2026 revenue up 13% to $846M as radiopharmaceutical and contrast demand grows alongside imaging volumes [1]
Cloud-first AI imaging platform strategy outlined at JPM 2026, aiming to orchestrate AI across enterprise imaging and deepen the installed-base moat [2]
key_risks: Low structural growth: 2020-2025 revenue CAGR of 3.7% and Q3 2026 organic orders growth of only 4.0% leave little room for execution slips [5][1]
Leverage from the spin: D/E ~90%, net debt/EBITDA ~2.4x and negative tangible book value constrain flexibility if hospital capital spending weakens [5]
Backlog eased from $23.9B to $23.7B with book-to-bill near 1.0x, and China/tariff exposure in imaging could pressure orders and margins [1]

backlog.note: Q3 2026 backlog of $23.7B, down slightly from the $23.9B record at Q2 2026; Q3 book-to-bill was 1.03x with organic orders +4.0%. TTM book-to-bill is not disclosed in the sources reviewed; quarterly ratios have held in the ~1.0-1.2x range, consistent with a yellow signal.
